title: how an agent finds out it under-captured
summary: An agent's own note count is the one thing it cannot check while writing, because kb write sees one spec at a time and never saw the worklist — so the worklist is handed forward out-of-band, through a tmpdir file keyed by session id, and comes back as a ratio printed with each write. The import graph cannot see this link at all: hooks/capture-payload.mjs (an .mjs hook) and src/kb/session-worklist.ts (the TS CLI) never import each other and agree only on a filename template, tmpdir/coldstart-kb-worklist-<sid>.json. Change the name or the record shape on one side and coverage silently stops printing — there is no error, because every read is best-effort by design.

steps.role: the one point every host passes through — writes the manifest (path, tier, needsNote) as a side effect of building the prompt
reads it back, records this write, computes done vs outstanding
prints the line under the write's own output, so it lands mid-Bash-block while the agent is still writing

invariants: The manifest filename and record shape are a contract between an .mjs hook and TS source that never import each other — change both sides together.
The session id the agent passes to `kb write --session` must be the same sid the capture prompt was built with, or there is no manifest and coverage is silent.
Silence is a valid outcome (no session, no manifest, stale, malformed) — coverage must never fail a write.
The denominator counts only files that needed a note; already-fresh files are excluded so full coverage stays reachable.
